# Executive Summary

<!--
This section provides a condensed view of the entire proposal, one page long.
It should be a comprehensive high-level overview that captures the essence of the proposal, including its goals, methods, expected outcomes, deliverables, and budget.
-->

R has good tooling for keeping code consistent, but nothing equivalent for the prose in a package: the help pages, vignettes, READMEs and comments.
Hard-to-read documentation costs users time and puts off newcomers, and there's more of it about as more package code and documentation gets written by AI tools.

[Vale](https://vale.sh) is the prose linter most other ecosystems have settled on.
Its rules are defined as data, there's a library of published styles, and it already integrates with editors, GitHub Actions and pre-commit.
It can read Markdown and pull the text out of comments in R files, but it doesn't know anything else about R.
Its default styles weren't written with R packages in mind, and using it at all means installing and configuring a binary by hand.

This proposal is for a Vale style for R package documentation, and an R package, valer, that installs Vale, writes the config for a project, and runs it from R.
The style picks out the rules from Vale's existing library that make sense for package docs, with thresholds set by running them over real CRAN packages and a vocabulary of R terms, so that the first run on a real package reports problems rather than noise.
The package also writes a block into a project's AGENTS.md so that AI coding agents run the linter on the documentation they write.

The deliverables are the style, published for anyone using Vale directly, and the package on CRAN, over two milestones ending in February 2027, for $3,600.
